COMMENT

THESE FORECASTS ASSUME A CONTINUATION OF PRESENT RESERVOIR RELEASES
AND ZERO QPF THROUGH 12Z TOMORROW MORNING.

SOME LIGHT SNOW WAS REPORTED OVER WESTERN BASINS DURING THE PAST 24
HOURS.

OTHER THAN ICE EFFECTS, MINOR CHANGES IN STAGE ARE FORECAST THROUGH
12Z TOMORROW MORNING.

THE TERM ICE EFFECTS MEANS THAT RIVER ICE ACCUMULATION IN THE
VICINITY OF THE RIVER GAGE IS ALTERING THE CHANNEL CROSS-SECTION (IN
ADDITION TO INCREASING FRICTION) WHICH PRODUCES HIGHER STAGES THAN
WOULD BE EXPECTED WITHOUT THE ICE.  THE RELATIONSHIP (RATING) BETWEEN
RIVER FLOW AND GAGE HEIGHT IS NO LONGER VALID.  A STRETCH OF RIVER
DOES NOT HAVE TO BE ICE COVERED TO EXHIBIT ICE EFFECTS.  ICE CAN FORM
ALONG THE SURFACE IN SLOW MOVING SECTIONS, ALONG THE BANKS AND SIDES
OF THE CHANNEL, AND ALSO ON THE CHANNEL BOTTOM (ANCHOR ICE).  ABRUPT
FLUCTUATIONS OF SEVERAL FEET ARE QUITE COMMON AND SHOULD BE EXPECTED
DURING EXTENDED COLD SPELLS.

MARFC
:...END of MESSAGE...
